newsitem.title: BRAZIL: RESEARCH ALERT-Petrobras still a buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Petrobras still a buy.

text.p: Robert Fleming & Co Ltd said it has reiterated its buy/positive rating for Brazilian state oil company Petrobras.

-- Fleming analysts Alan Marshall and Richard Griffith said the Senate's July 16 approval of Brazil's new oil sector deregulation bill frees Petrobras for joint ventures to develop the country's vast oil and gas reserves.
-- In a report, they also said Petrobras' selling prices for crude oil and refined products will soon come in line with the rest of the world.
-- "Already resource-rich, the new environment should allow Petrobras to increase both in size and value," they wrote.

-- Petrobras' "bull points" are its ranking as fifth-largest oil firm in the world in terms of reserves, its target of a 60-percent output rise from 1997 to 2000, its large offshore reserves and its oil and product price deregulation, they added.

-- They cited as "bear points" slower earnings and cash-flow growth due to possible deregulation delays, a lack of immediate plans for privatization or an ADR listing, limited transparency due to a lack of U.S. GAAP accounting methods and competition.
-- Petrobras' blue-chip preferred was 0.63 percent higher at 316.99 reais while its common was up 0.24 percent at 254.50 reais at 1632 local/1932 GMT in Sao Paulo.
